{"contradictions":[{"id":"C1","topic":"Whether the engagement rate is genuinely recovering, or whether the jump reflects the dormant-account closure shrinking the denominator","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":""Engagement is already recovering. The Programme Director treats the finding as still current; the programme members were surveyed about no longer exists in the same form. Wave 4 was scheduled for autumn 2024 and was not commissioned.","how_to_resolve":"Commission the deferred Wave 4 research against the post-January-2026 programme. Separately, measure the own-brand earn-rate cut and coupon retirement as an event study against 2026-Q1 and 2026-Q2 engagement, redemption and share-of-transaction rows."},{"id":"C7","topic":"Whether raising the earn rate is available as an intervention at all","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":""The research is clear. Members told us the earn rate on own-brand is what makes them scan. Put the earn rate back up and engagement moves."","locator":"Programme Director — Maeve Okonjo"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-0770c8bb","quote":"Any proposal that increases the cost of points earned or discounts given requires finance approval before a pilot may begin, and no net increase in promotional margin is available this year.","locator":"Priorities and constraints"},"summary":"The Programme Director proposes restoring the own-brand earn rate. Programme objectives state no net increase in promotional margin is available, and the Finance Director restated this at the review meeting including anything funded out of the points pool (EV-ed36a688). Both positions are on record and unreconciled.","how_to_resolve":"Ask finance whether a margin-neutral variant exists — for example an earn-rate restoration funded by withdrawing the everyday-low-pricing reduction it paid for. Note that any earn or redeem change requires 30 days' member notice under governance."},{"id":"C8","topic":"Whether the app usability problems have been fixed","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":""The app rebuild fixed the usability problems the 2023 study found. That is done. The next thing is personalisation off prescription data, because we know what people take."","locator":"Digital Lead — Priya Ravel"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-22f8864a","quote":"No usability study has been run against the rebuilt app.","locator":"2025-11-12 — App rebuild release"},"summary":"The Digital Lead asserts the 2023 usability problems are resolved. The operations log records that no usability study has been run against the rebuilt app, so the claim is untested. The 2023 finding was specific: only 3 of 42 interviewees could find their points balance without prompting.","how_to_resolve":"Run a usability study against the rebuilt app replicating the 2023 balance-finding task. Note also that real-time balance display is blocked by the read-only ledger feed refreshed every four hours (EV-1345e218)."},{"id":"C9","topic":"Whether prescription-data personalisation is a permitted next step","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":"The next thing is personalisation off prescription data, because we know what people take.","locator":"Digital Lead — Priya Ravel"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-630bd154","quote":"Dispensing records, prescription history and any data originating in the dispensary system may not be used for marketing segmentation, targeting or personalisation. Care Club membership consent does not cover this use.","locator":"Dispensing and prescription data"},"summary":"The Digital Lead proposes personalisation from prescription data. Governance prohibits exactly this use under existing membership consent and requires separate, explicit, purpose-specific consent recorded per member. Dispensing services are also listed as out of scope for FY26 in the programme objectives.","how_to_resolve":"Legal-privacy to confirm whether a per-member purpose-specific consent flow is feasible and what its expected capture rate would be, before any design work. Any health-condition inference additionally requires an approved DPIA with a six-week lead time."},{"id":"C10","topic":"Whether tiering is the differentiator to pursue, and the standing of the 19% figure","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":"The Programme Director circulated the 2024 competitive scan and highlighted the 19% visit-frequency figure attributed to Verity Health Stores, describing it as what tiering delivers.","locator":"Circulated material"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-dfa0856e","quote":"The figure comes from a Verity press release. No sample size, baseline, comparison group or measurement window is stated, and no independent evaluation has been published.","locator":"Claimed results"},"summary":"The 19% figure is being presented as evidence of what tiering delivers. The scan that carries the figure itself states it is an unevaluated competitor press-release claim with no baseline or comparison group. Separately, leadership already decided against tiering in FY26.","how_to_resolve":"Treat the 19% as unverified unless an independent evaluation surfaces. Reopening tiering would also require revisiting decision D-2025-06, which deferred it pending Pellworth integration and single-EPOS completion."},{"id":"C11","topic":"Whether the competitive scan's 'no paid tier' gap still holds","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-dfa0856e","quote":"No competitor in our catchment offers a paid or subscription tier.","locator":"Gaps in the market"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":"A colleague said that two of the three chains in the scan have launched paid tiers since it was written. Nobody could say which two, or when.","locator":"Circulated material"},"summary":"Both may be true of their own moments. The scan's desk research completed 2024-03-22 and its next refresh was scheduled for March 2025; the meeting note of 2026-07-21 asserts two of three chains have since launched paid tiers, but is unsourced and unspecific.","how_to_resolve":"Refresh the competitive scan, which is overdue by more than a year, and confirm which chains launched paid tiers and on what dates before treating the 'paid tier' gap as an available differentiator."},{"id":"C12","topic":"Which segment is the largest, and which is the largest engaged segment","kind":"scope_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-c8c04c10","quote":"segment: occasional_convenience

share_of_base_percent: 26.0
engagement_rate_percent: 21.0","locator":"member segmentation 2024 row 4"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-c7e1df16","quote":"segment: regular_prescription
members: 458000
share_of_base_percent: 20.2
engagement_rate_percent: 64.2","locator":"member segmentation 2024 row 1"},"summary":"Both 'largest' claims can be made and both are true of different segments. Occasional convenience is the largest segment by headcount at 587,000 members but engages at only 21.0%. Regular prescription is smaller at 458,000 but is the highest-engaging segment at 64.2% and so contributes the most engaged members. A recommendation citing 'the largest segment' must say which sense it means.","how_to_resolve":"State the target segment in headcount and engaged-member terms separately. Note the whole table is built on the base as at 30 June 2024 and has not been refreshed since, so it predates the Pellworth load and the dormant closure."},{"id":"C13","topic":"Whether the segmentation base is a valid description of the current membership","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-043ac12d","quote":"synthetic - built on the Care Club member base as at 30 June 2024 and not refreshed since","locator":"member segmentation 2024 row 6"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-dce9d700","quote":"period: 2026-Q2
metric: active_members_base
value: 1781000","locator":"engagement metrics row 18"},"summary":"The segmentation totals 2,262,000 members as at 30 June 2024. The current base is 1,781,000. In between, 251,000 Pellworth accounts were loaded and 918,000 accounts were closed, including the 530,000-member registered_only_or_dormant segment which the closure run would largely have removed.","how_to_resolve":"Rebuild the segmentation on the post-closure, post-migration base before using it to size any intervention."},{"id":"C14","topic":"Whether the till coupon should remain the default redemption route","kind":"temporal_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-31a8e867","quote":"Keep the till coupon as the default redemption route.","locator":"Recommendations"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-22f8864a","quote":"Coupon printing at the till was switched off in all stores on the same day the own-brand price change took effect.","locator":"2026-01-05 — Till coupon printing retired"},"summary":"The 2023 research recommended retaining the till coupon, on the basis that 79% of redemptions were made with a coupon printed at the till and members preferred it. That route was retired on 2026-01-05. The recommendation is not wrong for its period; it describes a mechanic that no longer exists. Points redemption rate falls from 47.9% in 2025-Q4 to 41.3% in 2026-Q1 to 38.6% in 2026-Q2.","how_to_resolve":"Test whether the redemption-rate decline across 2026-Q1 and 2026-Q2 is attributable to coupon retirement or to the concurrent earn-rate cut — the two changes landed on the same day, so the effects are confounded and cannot be separated from the existing series."},{"id":"C15","topic":"Whether engagement counts are complete","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-4d552aab","quote":"members with at least one earn or redeem event in the quarter - synthetic","locator":"engagement metrics row 1, note"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-fd0252d0","quote":"synthetic - not measured; the dispensing counter till does not write loyalty scans back to the member account","locator":"engagement metrics row 47"},"summary":"The engagement series is defined as members with at least one earn or redeem event, implying completeness. A companion row records that counter-only engaged members are not measured at all because the dispensing till does not write scans back. The operations log states the volume is not known, so the size of the undercount is unquantified.","how_to_resolve":"Instrument the dispensary till to write loyalty scans back, or run a manual reconciliation in a sample of stores to size the counter-only population, before treating engagement counts as complete."},{"id":"C16","topic":"Whether any of the proposed interventions can be measured or experimented on","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":"Whatever we did in the autumn worked, and we should do more of it.","locator":"Head of Retail Operations — Tomas Bright"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-1345e218","quote":"The rebuilt app has no feature-flag or A/B framework. Any experiment must be run as a manual store-level split, with allocation held in a spreadsheet by the analytics team.","locator":"Experimentation"},"summary":"A 'do more of what worked' recommendation presumes attribution. The platform has no A/B framework, member-level tables refresh only weekly, and 96 of 436 stores cannot read the Care Club barcode at all — so members in those stores cannot earn or redeem at the till and would contaminate any store-level split.","how_to_resolve":"Decide whether to wait for the 2026-Q4 EPOS migration before running store-level splits, or to design a split that excludes the 96 Pellworth-build stores. Either way, same-day measurement is not available."},{"id":"C17","topic":"Whether Pellworth-migrated members behave differently, and whether that is knowable","kind":"claim_conflict","side_a":{"evidence_id":"EV-ed36a688","quote":"Do the members who came from Pellworth Chemists behave differently from legacy members? Nobody in the room had the split.","locator":"Open question raised and not answered"},"side_b":{"evidence_id":"EV-22f8864a","quote":"251,000 Pellworth Chemists member accounts were loaded into the Care Club database and became addressable the same day.","locator":"2025-04-22 — Pellworth account migration"},"summary":"The question is unanswered in the room, but the operations record shows the cohort is identifiable: 251,000 accounts loaded on a known date, of which 214,000 were subsequently closed in October, leaving roughly 37,000 surviving migrated accounts. The engagement series carries no segment breakdown — every row is segment: all.","how_to_resolve":"Ask analytics to cut the engagement series by migration origin. Note the surviving migrated cohort is small relative to the base, and that 96 stores on the Pellworth EPOS build still cannot process Care Club scans, which would depress measured engagement for that cohort independently of behaviour."}]}

{"recommendation":{"statement":"Prioritise ALT-04: fix the measurement base first — restate the engagement series across the October 2025 dormant-account closure (and the April 2025 Pellworth load) so the trend is comparable, report engaged-member counts alongside the rate, and scope a scan-event-only write-back of dispensing-counter loyalty scans to the member account. Do this ahead of any member-facing change. The restatement is analyst work and should be delivered within weeks; the counter write-back should proceed only as a costed, legal-privacy-approved second step.
